catalogueDoc.summary: nanoGPT is a small, readable codebase for training and finetuning GPT language models. It includes a character-level Shakespeare demo that runs on a laptop CPU, plus recipes for reproducing GPT-2 on large GPU machines.

routes.title: Train a tiny model on Shakespeare and read what it writes
routes.description: Trains a small character-level GPT on CPU for a few minutes, then prints Shakespeare-like text sampled from it.

stepsSketch.cmd: pip install torch numpy transformers datasets tiktoken wandb tqdm

routes.title: Prompt the largest pretrained GPT-2 and read its answers
routes.description: Downloads OpenAI's GPT-2 XL weights and prints several continuations of a prompt.
routes.reason: needs far more than 4 GiB of RAM and a download of several GB for the 1.5B-parameter model

stepsSketch.cmd: python sample.py --init_from=gpt2-xl --start="What is the answer to life, the universe, and everything?" --num_samples=5 --max_new_tokens=100

routes.title: Finetune GPT-2 on Shakespeare and read the output
routes.description: Starts from a pretrained GPT-2 checkpoint and finetunes it on tiny Shakespeare.
routes.reason: needs a GPU and more memory than the sandbox has

routes.title: Reproduce GPT-2 (124M) training on OpenWebText
routes.description: Tokenizes the OpenWebText dataset and trains GPT-2 124M across eight GPUs for days.
routes.reason: needs multiple GPUs and a download of tens of GB

routes.title: Measure OpenWebText loss of the pretrained GPT-2 models
routes.description: Evaluates the OpenAI GPT-2 checkpoints on OpenWebText and reports train and validation loss.
routes.reason: needs the prepared OpenWebText dataset (tens of GB) and a GPU

routes.title: Benchmark training step speed of the GPT model
routes.description: Times the core training loop on synthetic data to measure iteration speed.
routes.reason: defaults target a GPU with a 124M-parameter model and large batches that exceed 4 GiB RAM
